title: Satpal Singh v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Abhinava Upadhya, J.; Shamim Ahmed, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed; petitioner relegated to Section 127 appeal.
headnote: Once a final assessment on an electricity-theft allegation has been made and a recovery certificate issued, the assessee’s remedy is an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The High Court will not entertain a writ petition in the face of that efficacious alternative remedy.
facts: On an allegation of electricity theft, a provisional assessment was made against the petitioner in 2018. He claimed to have filed an objection in 2019, well after the period prescribed under the Electricity Supply Code. A final assessment was thereafter made and a recovery certificate issued. He petitioned the Allahabad High Court. After an adjournment on 23 January 2020 with any interim order continued, the Division Bench heard the writ on 4 February 2020.

holding_units.topic: appeal against final assessment — alternative remedy bars writ
holding_units.holding: Where a final assessment has been made on an electricity-theft allegation and a recovery certificate issued, the petitioner has an efficacious remedy of appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003, and the High Court will not interfere in writ.

principle_tags.application: The Court dismissed the writ because an efficacious Section 127 appeal lay against the final assessment and the recovery certificate that followed.
Having recorded that a final assessment had been made and a recovery certificate issued, the Court held the petitioner to the Section 127 appeal and declined writ interference.

not_decided.point: Whether the 2019 objection to the 2018 provisional assessment was time-barred under the Electricity Supply Code
Validity or quantum of the final theft assessment, and legality of the recovery certificate
